description: This topic explains the chemical bonds formed between atoms and various types of chemical reactions. It is a crucial chapter under General Science for rapid revision and competitive exam preparation.

sections.title: Chemical Bonding
sections.description: The study of attractive forces holding atoms together, formed by the transfer or sharing of electrons.

key_concepts.explanation: Atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons until they have 8 electrons in their valence shell, achieving a stable noble gas electronic configuration.
A bond formed by the complete transfer of one or more electrons from one atom to another. Example: Sodium Chloride (NaCl).
A bond formed by the equal sharing of electrons between two atoms. Examples: Methane (CH4) and Water (H2O).
A type of covalent bond where the shared pair of electrons is provided by only one of the participating atoms. Also known as a Donor-Acceptor bond.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: The tendency of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons in a covalent bond towards itself.
scientific_principles.application: Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table.

important_facts.fact: Ionic compounds have very high melting and boiling points and are good conductors of electricity in their molten or aqueous state.
Covalent compounds are generally bad conductors of electricity, but Graphite is a notable exception.

sections.title: Types of Chemical Reactions
sections.description: Classification of chemical changes and molecular rearrangements that occur when substances interact.

key_concepts.explanation: A reaction in which two or more reactants combine to form a single product. (A + B → AB)
A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products under the influence of heat, light, or electricity. (AB → A + B)
A reaction where a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
A reaction involving an exchange of ions between two reactants, typically resulting in the formation of an insoluble precipitate.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a balanced chemical reaction.
scientific_principles.application: Total mass of reactants = Total mass of products.

sections.title: Reactions based on Thermodynamics
sections.description: Classification of chemical reactions based on the absorption or evolution of heat energy.

key_concepts.explanation: A reaction in which heat is released along with the formation of products. Examples: Respiration, Combustion of natural gas.
A reaction that requires the absorption of energy (in the form of heat, light, or electricity) to break down the reactants. Example: Photosynthesis.

sections.title: Oxidation and Reduction (Redox)
sections.description: Reactions based on the transfer of electrons and the addition or removal of oxygen/hydrogen.

key_concepts.explanation: The addition of oxygen, removal of hydrogen, or the loss of electrons from a substance.
The addition of hydrogen, removal of oxygen, or the gain of electrons by a substance.
A chemical reaction in which oxidation and reduction processes occur simultaneously.

key_associations.extra_info: A substance that oxidizes other substances and gets reduced itself.
A substance that reduces other substances and gets oxidized itself.

important_facts.fact: Rusting of iron is a slow oxidation reaction that occurs in the presence of moisture and oxygen.
Rancidity is caused by the oxidation of fats and oils in food, which is prevented by flushing packets with antioxidants like Nitrogen gas.

sections.title: Catalysis and Industrial Reactions
sections.description: Substances that alter the rate of a reaction and their specific uses in large-scale industrial processes.

key_concepts.explanation: An external substance that alters (usually speeds up) the rate of a chemical reaction without undergoing any permanent chemical change itself.

key_associations.extra_info: Molybdenum (Mo) is used alongside as a catalyst promoter to increase efficiency.

key_associations.item: Sulfuric Acid (H2SO4) production by Contact Process
key_associations.extra_info: A highly crucial industrial catalytic process for acid manufacturing.
The process of converting unsaturated liquid fats into saturated solid fats (Vanaspati Ghee).

important_facts.fact: Enzymes act as bio-catalysts, regulating complex biochemical reactions in living organisms.
